newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's stock market depressed by Iraq, Israel.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's stock market depressed by Iraq, Israel.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.12 percent on Saturday in subdued trade, depressed by vocal opposition to last week's Israeli trade fair in Amman and a delay in renewing Jordan's annual trade protocol with Iraq, traders said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.19 points to 152.88 points in meagre turnover worth 307,000 dinars ($436,000).
"There was uncertainty caused by the events at the Israeli fair. It has a psychological effect," said analyst Mohammed Abdullah from Pearl Investment.
Jordanian unions called for a one-hour work stoppage on Thursday to protest the first Israeli trade exhibition to be held in Jordan.
The protests followed increasing popular hostility in Jordan towards Israel despite a 1994 peace accord, which Jordanians say has brought few economic benefits.
Abdullah said delays in agreeing this year's trade protocol between Amman and Bahgdad also weighed on the market, which surged last month when Iraq's U.N.-approved oil-for-food deal was announced.
But trucking firm Unified Land Transport, expected to benefit from any increase in shipments to Iraq, fell more than three percent to 2.12 dinars in trade worth nearly 40,000 dinars.
The Housing Bank, the busiest stock in Saturday's quiet market with turnover worth 83,000 dinars, bucked the downward slide with slight gain to 4.80 dinars.
But overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 27 to four. Shares in another two companies traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.19 percent to 82.56 points from 82.72 points.
